intent: The picture inside an Avatar, rendered only once it has loaded.
typical_uses: A person's or account's profile picture inside an Avatar

dont_use_when.situation: A picture that is not someone's avatar

instead.note: AvatarImage renders nothing until a separate load succeeds and requires an Avatar root around it; an ordinary image needs neither.

invariants.text: The img enters the DOM only when the load status becomes loaded; while the image is idle, loading or has failed AvatarImage renders nothing. When the status leaves loaded the img carries `data-ending-style` and is removed once its animations finish, and avatar.module.css declares none on it.

The load status comes from a separate `window.Image` the primitive creates with the same `src`, `srcSet`, `sizes`, `crossOrigin` and `referrerPolicy`, not from the rendered img; with neither `src` nor `srcSet` the status is error at once.

Changing `src`, `srcSet`, `sizes`, `crossOrigin` or `referrerPolicy` starts a new load: the status goes back to loading and the fallback shows until the new load succeeds, except for an image the browser already has cached, which reports loaded in the same pass.
`onLoadingStatusChange` is called with loading, loaded or error as the status changes; it is never called with idle, including when the AvatarImage unmounts and the root's status returns to idle.

anti_patterns.dont: Style or animate the img expecting it to be present while it loads
anti_patterns.do_instead: Style the loading state on AvatarFallback - the img does not exist until the load has succeeded

a11y.by: the primitive's Avatar.Image renders a native img carrying the consumer's `alt`; avatar.test.tsx asserts getByAltText('Jane Doe') finds it once loaded ("hides the fallback and renders the image once it loads") and queryByAltText('Jane Doe') is null after a failed load ("falls back when the image fails to load")

onLoadingStatusChange.states: onLoadingStatusChange is a callback called with the image's new load status, not a value
onLoadingStatusChange.because: `(status: ImageLoadingStatus) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the image's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the image's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (imageLoadingStatus, transitionStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through avatar.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: An image with no Avatar root around it
bad.why: The primitive's Avatar.Image reads the root's context to report its load status and throws when no Avatar is above it.
